question.text: Mahaganga Infrastructure Fund (Cat II AIF) pays INR 15 crore of investment management fees to its Investment Manager SPV in FY25. What is the GST treatment?

answer.text: GST at 5% concessional rate, borne by the IM
GST at 18% on the management fee, levied on the supply by the Investment Manager to the Fund — the Fund bears the GST cost (typically no input-tax-credit at the Fund level)
Exempt — financial services to AIFs are nil-rated
GST at 28% as a luxury service

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook Para 16.7: GST at 18% applies to investment management and trusteeship fees supplied by the IM/Trustee to the Fund. The Fund bears the 18% since it generally cannot claim input-tax-credit (its outward supplies of investment returns are not taxable supplies under GST). At INR 15 cr fee: 18% = INR 2.7 cr GST. The Trap: Option A — 5% is not an AIF-relevant rate. Option C — AIF services are NOT exempt; financial services exemption is narrow. Option D — 28% is for sin/luxury goods. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C covers GST broadly; XIX-C tests economic impact on LP net returns. Manager's Pro-Tip: When quoting net returns to LPs, show them the 'GST drag': ~18% x fee = real leakage. IFSC-GIFT funds get partial GST relief — if you run parallel onshore + GIFT feeders, allocate high-fee items to the GIFT feeder where possible.
